title: Physiological World Models for Human State Transitions
abstract: arXiv:2608.15309v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continuous multimodal sensing now allows human physiology to be observed throughout daily life rather than only during occasional clinical visits. However, most health artificial intelligence systems are designed to recognize current states, estimate risks or analyse individual biomarkers. They do not directly model how physiological states change in response to real-world events, behaviours, contexts and interventions. Here we propose the Physiological World Model (PWM), an event-conditioned framework for learning these changes at the level of the whole person. We introduce the HumanState Transition Token, a structured, quality-scored unit that connects the physiological state before an event with the event or action, relevant context and intervention information, the physiological trajectory after the event, observed outcomes and data quality. translated_title: 生理世界模型用于人类状态转换
translated_abstract: 连续的多种模态感知现在使得人类生理状态可以在日常生活中被观察，而不仅仅是在偶尔的临床访问中。然而，大多数健康人工智能系统旨在识别当前状态、评估风险或分析单个生物标志物。它们并不直接建模生理状态如何响应现实世界事件、行为、情境和干预而变化。在这里，我们提出了生理世界模型（PWM），一种事件条件化框架，用于在整个人体水平上学习这些变化。我们引入了人类状态转换令牌，一个结构化、质量评分的单元，它将事件前的生理状态与事件或动作、相关情境和干预信息、事件后的生理轨迹、观察结果和数据质量联系起来。我们描述了四个能力级别，从状态表示到有界干预规划。
tldr: 本文提出了一种事件条件化的生理世界模型，通过引入人类状态转换令牌，首次实现了对日常生理状态在真实事件驱动下变化的整体建模，支持从状态识别到有界干预规划的能力提升。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an event-conditioned Physiological World Model that, for the first time, enables holistic modeling of daily physiological state transitions driven by real-world events via a structured HumanState Transition Token, advancing capabilities from state recognition to bounded intervention planning.
